scope: The town halls/administrative seats of the 23 Berlin boroughs immediately before the 2001 merger; all 12 present borough main seats are among these sites.
geometryPolicy: Semantic identity references only. Coordinates, footprints, roofs and measured heights come from townhall-osm-v227.json and townhall-source-v227.json. Facade subdivisions and colors without explicit source tags remain display estimates. Do not reconstruct demolished predecessors or unbuilt extensions.

sites.name: Rathaus Mitte
sites.status: Existing district administration; the present merged district's main seat is Rathaus Tiergarten.
cues: 1998 administrative high-rise with horizontal window/concrete bands and a glazed stairwell
Rear assembly pavilion; not the former Hotel Berolina or a future Rathaus at Haus der Statistik

sites.name: Rathaus Tiergarten
sites.status: Existing main seat of the merged district Mitte.
cues: Five-storey civic block with recessed honor court and portico facing Turmstraße
Preserve the court and actual roof; no invented Rathaus clocktower

sites.name: Rathaus Wedding
sites.status: Existing former district town hall and later administrative extension.
cues: Plain red clinker main block from 1929–30
Distinct 1964–66 modern extension/high-rise and assembly hall; do not give the extension the old block's brick treatment

sites.name: Rathaus Friedrichshain
sites.status: Existing main administrative/mayoral address of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg.
cues: Modern office building: use its retained source envelope, actual roof and facade tags
No independently verified historic tower or ornament; source-bound regular facade fittings remain estimates

sites.name: Rathaus Kreuzberg
sites.status: Existing municipal office/BVV site; not the current district mayor's principal address.
cues: Retain the source office block and its separate parts
Do not confuse the adjacent Dragoner barracks in the Rathausblock with the Rathaus itself; unsurveyed window divisions remain estimates

sites.name: Rathaus Pankow
sites.status: Existing main town hall of merged Pankow.
cues: Broad red clinker and red sandstone main building with granite base
Projecting center with three entrance arches and columns; corner clocktower with balcony bays, balustrade, cylindrical upper stage and lantern
The original copper main roof was removed historically; retain the measured present roof rather than reconstructing the original

sites.name: Bezirksamt Prenzlauer Berg / Fröbelstraße
sites.status: Existing municipal campus in the former hospital and hospice ensemble; several buildings, not one invented freestanding town hall.
cues: Retain mapped campus buildings, courtyards and distinct source roofs
Hospital ensemble dates to 1886–89; houses 6 and 9 and gatehouse are separate 1896 additions
House 6 is documented for district administration; temporary moves to house 9 do not justify moving the complete Rathaus identity there. Material and window estimates must remain labeled

sites.name: Rathaus Weißensee / Askaniahaus
sites.status: Former district Rathaus in the Askania factory administration ensemble; present Bürgeramt.
cues: Office/factory ensemble with administrative building and hall from 1940–41; use the measured envelope
Do not substitute a picturesque medieval town hall from the unrelated town Weißensee; no invented clocktower or speculative facade material

sites.name: Rathaus Charlottenburg
sites.status: Existing main town hall of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf.
cues: Ornamented sandstone street facade with Jugendstil details and clocktower
Street roofs with red tiles, courtyard roofs with slate; the 1911–13 extension is more restrained
Retain measured tower and roof geometry; published overall heights are not replacement dimensions

sites.name: Ehemaliges Rathaus Wilmersdorf
sites.status: Existing former Rathaus, not the merged district's main seat; specific present tenancy is not asserted.
cues: 1941–43 masonry complex with rounded inner court and horizontal divisions; Tuscan columns in the court
Do not reconstruct the destroyed predecessor at Brandenburgische Straße or the unbuilt Preußenpark Rathaus plan

sites.name: Rathaus Spandau
sites.status: Existing main district town hall.
cues: 1910–13 town hall with tall clocktower and four clock faces
Keep the present surveyed tower crown and roof; do not restore destroyed historic elements from old photographs

sites.name: Rathaus Steglitz
sites.status: Existing former district town hall and present municipal site.
cues: 1896–97 town hall with 1934 alteration; preserve the existing dedicated brick/gable/spire recognition
Keep the complete source sheets and distinct roof parts; no unverified numeric tower-height override

sites.name: Rathaus Zehlendorf
sites.status: Existing main municipal campus; proposed extension is not an existing building.
cues: Three-wing 1926–29 administrative scheme, column arcade, loggia and large civic hall windows
Explicitly designed without a Rathaus tower; retain actual campus buildings instead of filling the whole site polygon
Competition and future extension plans do not authorize future volumes

sites.name: Rathaus Schöneberg
sites.status: Existing main district town hall.
cues: Four-storey plaster building above high sandstone base, colossal Ionic pilasters, high hipped roofs and multiple courts
Clock/bell tower's postwar crown has open sound bays; do not reconstruct the destroyed original cupola

sites.name: Rathaus Tempelhof
sites.status: Existing former district town hall and municipal site; future Neue Mitte Tempelhof plans excluded.
cues: Four-storey old building and lower 1960 extension are distinct source parts
Keep measured roofs and tower-like masses without adding a guessed historic tower; the low extension is not treated as the old facade

sites.name: Rathaus Neukölln
sites.status: Existing main district town hall.
cues: Light stone facade, red roofs and green copper clocktower crown with Fortuna weather figure
Retain postwar wings as built; documented overall tower-height differences are not geometry instructions

sites.name: Rathaus Treptow
sites.status: Existing former district town hall, current municipal/BVV site.
cues: 1909–10 Renaissance-influenced town hall; keep existing irregular source building and roofs
Distinct from the merged district's main Rathaus Köpenick; facade subdivisions not measured in the reference remain estimates

sites.name: Rathaus Köpenick
sites.status: Existing main district town hall, with 2026 reopening after refurbishment.
cues: Brick Gothic town hall, ornamental gables, tracery and glazed bricks
Preserve corner tower and all 1901–04/1920s/1930s source wings; retained dedicated model remains authoritative

sites.name: Rathaus Marzahn
sites.status: Existing listed former district town hall and municipal offices.
cues: 1985–88 civic building by Eisentraut, Bock and Walther at the square's north edge
Keep distinctive measured massing and roof articulation; material/window details beyond retained tags remain display estimates, with no added medieval clocktower

sites.name: Rathaus Hellersdorf / Marzahn-Hellersdorf
sites.status: Existing main administrative seat of Marzahn-Hellersdorf.
cues: Modern Rathaus within Helle Mitte; retain measured block/courtyard and regular window character
No independently verified historical tower or exact color specification; material and subdivision estimates remain labeled

sites.name: Rathaus Lichtenberg
sites.status: Existing main district town hall.
cues: Red brick town hall from 1898 with retained source gables and roof
Keep present roof and upper masses; no conjectural restoration of a former crown

sites.name: Bezirksamt Hohenschönhausen / Große-Leege-Straße
sites.status: Existing former borough administration and current municipal/Bürgeramt site.
cues: Preserve actual modern office envelope and facade tags with modest source-bound regular window fittings
This is not the old village Rathaus at Hauptstraße 50; no invented ornamental tower

sites.name: Rathaus Reinickendorf / Rathaus Wittenau
sites.status: Existing main district town hall with modern extension and Ernst-Reuter-Saal.
cues: Red brick and shell limestone, curved Dutch-Baroque gables, bays and clocktower
1950s south extension and Ernst-Reuter-Saal retain their separate modern character; do not apply old brick ornament to every part
Published tower heights vary; retain measured source geometry
